proposals.before: The emperor said: "Rites value hitting the mean; excess is extravagance, shortfall is austerity—the previous dynasty judged this with precision.
proposals.after: The emperor said: "Rites value hitting the mean; excess is extravagance, shortfall is austerity—the previous court judged this with precision.
proposals.reason: 先朝 means the previous court/reign (Hongwu), not a previous dynasty.

proposals.before: Since the Nine Dragons carriage did not exist in the previous dynasty, let things remain as they are."
proposals.after: Since the Nine Dragons carriage did not exist under the previous court, let things remain as they are."
proposals.reason: 先朝 means the previous court/reign, not a previous dynasty.

proposals.before: Duty commandants each wore goose-down caps, single-layer grandson garments, copper belts, and full sets of boots and shoes.
proposals.after: Duty commandants each wore goose-down caps, jisun garments, copper belts, and full sets of boots and shoes.
proposals.reason: 只孫衣 is the Yuan-Ming ceremonial jisun/zhison robe, not garments related to a grandson.

proposals.before: The guard commandants on duty each wore goose-down caps, single-layer grandson garments, copper belts, and one set each of boots, shoes, and sandals.
proposals.after: The guard commandants on duty each wore goose-down caps, jisun garments, copper belts, and one set each of boots, shoes, and sandals.
proposals.reason: 只孫衣 is the ceremonial jisun robe, not “grandson garments”.

proposals.before: The heir apparent's ceremonial train followed the same rules.
proposals.after: A prince's heir's ceremonial train followed the same rules.
proposals.reason: 世子 is the heir of an imperial prince, not the heir apparent (皇太子).

proposals.before: The heir apparent's ceremonial regalia was the same in all respects.
proposals.after: A prince's heir's ceremonial regalia was the same in all respects.
proposals.reason: 世子 denotes a prince’s heir, not the crown prince.

proposals.before: Imperial princesses and heirs' consorts followed the same rules.
proposals.after: Imperial princesses and consorts of princes' heirs followed the same rules.
proposals.reason: 世子妃 is the consort of a prince’s heir (世子), not of the heir apparent.

proposals.before: Imperial princesses and consorts of heirs apparent had the same ceremonial regalia.
proposals.after: Imperial princesses and consorts of princes' heirs had the same ceremonial regalia.
proposals.reason: 世子妃 refers to consorts of princes’ heirs, not heirs apparent.

decisions.reason: Yongle is speaking within the Ming; 先朝 refers to the preceding Hongwu court/reign, not another dynasty, so 'previous court' is the accurate literal.
Same 先朝 as in s0087: the Nine Dragons carriage was absent under the previous Ming court, not under a prior dynasty; 'previous court' restores the sense.
只孫衣 is the Yuan–Ming ceremonial jisun robe (a loanword garment name), not 'single-layer grandson garments'; the proposed 'jisun garments' corrects the mistranslation.
Literal likewise misread 只孫 as 'grandson'; replacing with 'jisun garments' matches the ceremonial robe term in the Chinese.

decisions.after: The ceremonial train of a prince's heir followed the same rules.
decisions.reason: Following 親王儀仗, 世子 is a prince's heir, not the heir apparent (皇太子); the proposal's sense is right, but stacked 'prince's heir's' is awkward, so rephrase.

decisions.after: The ceremonial regalia of a prince's heir was the same in all respects.
decisions.reason: 世子 after 親王 is a prince's heir, not the crown prince; keep that correction but avoid the awkward double possessive in the proposal.
After 親王妃 and distinct from 東宮妃 in s0115, 世子妃 are consorts of princes' heirs; the proposed wording correctly separates them from the heir apparent.
世子妃 means consorts of 世子 (princes' heirs), not of heirs apparent; the literal repair matches the Chinese and the surrounding rank sequence.
